ACCOUNTING

                           8244
                     Paper 1



1.             GENERAL COMMENTS
The overall standard of the learners’ work has improved although there are still some learners who were not able to cope
with the demands of Accounting AS level.

 A point of concern, however, is the preparation of the General Journal:  teachers should teach the learners the proper
way to prepare the General Journal.

Teachers are encouraged to continue emphasizing the importance of dates, names of contra accounts, layout of
Statements, etc.  It is also of vital importance that learners are taught to show their calculations.   It is important that
teachers ensure that the entire syllabus is taught.

Some learners struggled to finish the paper and teachers are encouraged to teach time-management skills in answering
an examination paper during the year.

Learners misinterpreted some of the questions and did not answer what was asked. Teachers are requested to
encourage learners to read the questions carefully and only answer what is asked. Some learners could not apply their
knowledge to the questions asked.

The neatness of the learners’ work has improved.  Learners must make their digits clear and legible.   Abbreviations are
not allowed.

      (b)   Well answered.  Although most learners could state two features of a partnership agreement, some
            learners only refer to interest on loan and failed to indicate that only interest on loans from partners
            will be stated in the agreement.
            Answer
            -  The venue of the business premises and the name of the accountant, solicitors and bank, acting
               on behalf of the business.
            -  How the profits and losses of the business are to be shared by the partners.
            -  How salaries or drawings are to be arranged.
            -  Whether interest is to be paid on capital accounts.
            -  Whether interest is to be charged on any drawings.
            -  The rate of interest to be paid on any loans provided by partners.
            -  Any aspects concerning control and responsibilities by partners.
            -  The procedure in the event of admittance of a new partner or the departure of an existing partner.
            -  The procedure in the event of dissolution.
            -  Amount of capital contribution by each partner.                                                               Any two [2]

3.                     POSITIVE SUGGESTIONS TO TEACHERS
Teachers should differentiate between the different levels of questions and how to approach the level C and D questions.

Learners should show all workings and calculations in additional to explaining terminology in full sentences.
Pay attention to dates, the correct account names and the correct layouts.

Learners should be coached to read the questions with care and understanding.

Do not only work from old examination papers, as it appears that learners tend to be threatened by questions with a
different format.

Teachers must plan enough time for revision and examination preparation.  Pay attention to terminology.

Teachers should coach learners to read carefully and with understanding, especially the requirements to a question,
and to answer only what is asked.

1.    GENERAL COMMENTS
Again in 2023 there were a lot of learners who wrote the examination.  We still found that almost all the learners
who received a C grading on Ordinary level struggled to cope.  That again led to a huge number of learners with low
marks. There again were 40 marks related to theory questions in the paper and we could see that most of the learners
interpreted them incorrectly.  Especially the “advise” end “analyse” questions.

Another concern is the fact that one could see that a lot of centres did not finish the syllabus.  It is very important to know
that nearly half of Paper 2 marks are allocated to managerial accounting.  A serious mistake is that although managerial
accounting   is   in   the   last   part   of   the   syllabus   that   teachers   will   do   managerial   accounting   first   in   the   beginning   of   the
year and then the rest of the syllabus.  Too many learners loose marks in the questions about managerial accounting
because it was not done or taught to them.

3.     POSITIVE SUGGESTIONS TO TEACHERS
It is highly recommended that teachers must teach the managerial accounting first.  It is about 50 marks of Paper
2 so it is very important that the learners must be taught well in managerial accounting.

We could see that learners are well prepared to do the bookkeeping part of the paper but they will need practice on
how   to   answer   theory   questions.      Old   papers   (also   the   Higher   Grade   papers)   will   help.      Learners   must   be   told   of   the
importance of being able to answer theory questions because that is a big part of the AS papers.

We could see that the teachers are busy gaining the upper hand on the new syllabus.  Most of the work is improving and
that shows the input of the teachers.

Generally, the performance in this paper was slightly better compared to last year.  However, questions that required
calculations still proved to be difficult for most candidates e.g. Question 5(d) and Question 6(a).  Teachers still need to

for  Question  12  (which  was  on Agricultural  Economics).   This  is  as  indication  that  this  topic  is  still  a  challenge  to  most
candidates.     Teachers   are   urged   to   allocate   more   revision   time   to   this   topic   in   future.     Teachers   are   also   encouraged
to continue emphasising the importance of command words and train learners to read questions carefully and with
understanding for them to be able to interpret the question requirements correctly as well as answer the questions
appropriately.  Candidates still need to be reminded of the importance of clear handwriting and how to delete incorrect

GENERAL COMMENTS
Many centres submitted the required documents and worksheets of good standard for external moderation.  Some
worksheets submitted were, however, not of acceptable standard.  Most Centres submitted evidence in the form of
pictures as required.  Centres are encouraged to ensure that pictures submitted as evidence for practical investigations
are       attached       to       specific       investigation       reports.              Pictures       must       be       clear       enough       and       should       show       all       stages       of       the
investigation with candidates busy carrying out the tasks.

Investigation topics selected by candidates at some centres were still not of investigative nature.  Teachers need
to ensure that practical investigations topics selected by candidates are of investigative nature, meaning candidates
should  find  information  for  themselves  by  direct  observation  and  measurement.    See page 26 of Agricultural Science
NSSCAS syllabus.

Candidates who are submitting typed reports are advised to use Arial / Times New Roman font and                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          font size 12 with
1.5 line spacing.

Appropriateness of Assessment Tasks
Many Centres managed to select practical tasks from different themes outlined in the syllabus.  Some centres selected
simple tasks that are not challenging enough for candidates at this level.  Candidates should not only prepare seedbeds
but should also grow some vegetables on the prepared plots and take care of them till harvesting and marketing.
Similarly, for the task on seed germination, which was selected by most Centres, candidates should grow the viable
seedlings and take care of them until harvesting time as well.  Soil pH should be broaden to regulation of the soil pH
when the soil is tested.  A food sample should be tested for at least two or more nutrients. Alternatively, different samples
can be tested for one nutrient.

Some centres selected topic tasks that were more of an investigation e.g. tropism, spinach shelf life.  Tasks should be
hands-on, allowing candidates to apply their technical skills e.g. use tools and apparatus.  Some tasks did not assess
any practical skills as they were only addressing assessment objective B. e.g. Cash flow statement.

Interpretation and application of assessment criteria
Most centres were aware of the five assessment criteria that should be assessed in each practical task and there was
a great improvement in the generation of marking points per marking criteria.

Centres are urged to develop more challenging practical-based questions under the written component of the worksheets.
Teachers are reminded that written work completed by candidates is important evidence that they have participated in
by carrying out of a specific assessment task.

Suitability and relevance of practical investigations

Selection of relevant question (hypothesis) for the investigation
Many candidates were able to come up with a hypothesis for their investigation.  However, some candidates selected
topics that were not experimental e.g. surveys like Impacts of Covid19 on fish factories.  Some were not of investigative
nature  e.g.  processing  of  cheese.    Selected  topics  should  be  of  investigative  nature,  meaning  candidates  should  find
information for themselves by direct observation and measurement.  See page 26 of Agricultural Science NSSCAS
syllabus.

Planning of the investigation
It was evident that centres that did prior planning, produced investigations of acceptable standard.  Candidates at some
centres   opted   for   topics   with   more   than   one   variable   but   failed   to   attend   to   all   the   variables   e.g.   influence   of   organic
fertilizer on germination, growth and yield but only collected data on germination.  Some investigations required to
have a control e.g. the effect of manure on plant growth.  A control plot was required for comparative reason to make
reasonable deductions.  Most candidates could not replicate their work. Replication of treatments is necessary to reduce
the risk of failure.

Handling of evidence
Most candidates showed understanding of how to handle data collected through completed tables and graphs.  However,
some candidates failed to label and scale their graphs correctly.  Results presented by some candidates seemed
unrealistic.  Candidates whose reports are handwritten are encouraged to use graph paper for plotting graphs.

Ability to make deductions
Most candidates could interpret and analyse their data.  Deductions (conclusions) made by some candidates were,
however, not linked to the data collected or hypothesis.

Limitations
Most candidates were able to identify 1 or 2 limitations experienced during their investigations.  Some recommendations
suggested      by      candidates      were      not      addressing      the      identified      limitations.            Centres      should      encourage      candidates      to
suggest improvements that will help future researchers to overcome the identified limitations.

Presentation, layout and originality
Many candidates were able to follow the report layout as outlined in the syllabus.  However, some candidates did not
indicate the duration of their practical investigations.  Candidates need proper guidance on how to write methodology.
Some candidates’ methodologies were not clearly describing what their investigations were all about.  Candidates
were leaving out the most important part of the methodology which is description of treatment e.g. how the plots were
treated, how it was done, what was applied. Methodology should give a clear insight into what the investigation is all
about.  Candidates are urged to use pictures from their own investigations rather than using downloaded pictures from
the internet.

Interpretation and application of assessment criteria for practical investigations
Most centres were able to interpret and apply the assessment criteria for practical investigation with regards to the six
marking criteria.  Few centres did not, however, use the assessment criteria stipulated in the syllabus to award marks.
Centres are urged to use the assessment criteria for practical investigations when awarding marks for candidates’
practical investigations and to provide annotations as to how the marks were awarded.

Administration
It is appreciated that many centres complied with all the administrative procedures that are required for moderation
purposes and that some centres put in extra effort by providing the required information in neat and well-organised files.
This made the moderation exercise much easier.

Some errors in addition of marks were, however, detected.  Centres' internal moderators should not only moderate and
verify marks in the Assessment Summary form but are urged to also ensure that marks are correctly transferred from
the Individual Record Cards to the Assessment Summary form and later to the MS1 form.
There was an improvement by most centres in submitting evidence of candidates’ work in the form of pictures, showing
all the main stages of the practical tasks and not just the end result.

It is important to verify before sealing the envelope that all the necessary documents for external moderation are
enclosed in the envelope.
Centres are referred to the reverse side of the Individual Record Cards, Coursework Assessment Summary Forms for
additional information.

In conclusion, the performance demonstrated by candidates was satisfactory.  We recommend that training be arranged
by     Regional     Offices     for     Centres.         Agricultural     Science    Advanced     Subsidiary     level     teachers     should     seek     assistance
regarding the conducting and administering of School-Based Assessment in Agricultural Science.

COMMENTS ACCORDING TO THE ASSESSMENT OBJECTIVES.

A:  Research and record

Learners should be encouraged to conduct proper investigation and research on a variety of appropriate sources.  It
seems that investigation was not done, therefore, the chosen topic was not clear.  Ideas, observations and insights
should always be recorded visually and in written form.  This should be relevant to the learner’s intentions and the
learner    must    reflect    critically    on    work    as    well    as    the    progress    thereof.        This    means    thought    processes    must    always
be recorded.  It is advisable that learners should have a starting point, showing development through different ideas
towards the final.  It seems that learners did not use a variety of appropriate  sources that lead to more than one idea.
Therefore it leads to poor marks.

Because of a lack of research and recording the learners are not able to reflect critically on work and progress.

B:  Explore and select

Because of a lack of research and investigation of a variety of appropriate sources in assessment objective A, it is
impossible for learners to explore and select from resources. In this assessment ideas should be reviewed and refined
as the work develops, but because of a lack of a variety of resources it cannot be done.

It should be remembered that media materials and techniques should also be refined and developed.

C:  Develop ideas

Again, because of a lack of research, recording, exploration and selection of a variety of appropriate sources, ideas
cannot be developed and refined through sustained and focused investigation.  Personal thoughts, ideas and intentions
should be referenced from sources used. This is only possible through analytical and critical understanding.

D:  Produce

If  the  learner  does  not  demonstrate  analytical  and  critical  understanding,  it  is  very  difficult  to  produce  a  personal  and
meaningful response that shows the intentions of the learner.

      (b) (i)     There are many misconceptions about the working of the antibiotic amongst the learners.
                  Bacterial cells have cell walls made of peptidoglycans, which are long molecules containing chains of
                  amino acids and sugars.
                  In a bacterial cell wall the peptidoglycans are held together by cross-links which form between them.
                  The antibiotics prevent the formation of peptidoglycan and inhibit the enzyme which build the cross-
                  links.  These antibiotics are only active against bacteria while they are growing.
                  When a newly formed bacterial cell is growing, it secretes enzymes, called autolysins, which make
                  holes in its cell wall.  These little holes allow the wall to stretch so that new peptidoglycan chains can
                  link together.  The antibiotic prevents this linking, but the autolysins keep on making new holes.  This
                  causes the cell wall to become weaker.
                  Since bacteria live in watery environments, they take up water by osmosis.  When the cell wall is
                  weakened, it cannot withstand the higher / increasing osmotic pressure inside the cell, which puts
                  pressure on the cell wall, and the cell bursts.
                  reference to preventing the synthesis of peptidoglycan / weakens the cell wall;  AW

Positive suggestions to teachers
Biology teachers/laboratory technicians must be conversant with the techniques to prepare solutions and materials
required for the practical examination or work in corroboration with the Chemistry teachers.
Candidates should be introduced to the standard operating procedures (SOP) of the laboratory to know how to handle
the chemicals and equipments especially during the national examination. Candidates who have used materials and
apparatus during practical work throughout the year as part of the course are likely to perform better in the examination.
Whilst the activities in the examination may not be familiar, candidates who have had the opportunity to follow instructions
carefully in a variety of practical work are likely to find it easier to organise and complete unfamiliar activities.
Preparing        the        correct        materials        and        providing        the        specified        apparatus        are        critical        for        the        success        of        the
examination.
•    It is recommended that candidates should be given the opportunity to experience a variety of practical work
     throughout the year, in order to develop the skills that can be applied to the requirements of the examination, for
     example, candidates should be exposed to the microscope, they should be able to estimate a concentration by
     serial dilution by the factor of 10 each time or reduce the concentration of the solution by half each time or simple
     dilution.
•    Candidates should be encouraged always to read the questions and understand them before they attempt to
     answer them. The word 'describe' requires candidates to state in words the main points of the topic and what should
     be used. It is often used with reference either to particular phenomena or to particular experiments.

presentation of an argument and it is advised that a concise range of vocabulary is incorporated into responses that
demonstrates candidate’s high level of understanding.  Lengthier responses or the inclusion of more details than
required by a question sometimes led to contradictions in candidate answers.  In addition, some candidates elect to
commit their reasoning to paper, which is reasonable for ‘describe’ or ‘explain’ questions, but there is always the risk of
introducing a contradiction.  For example, in Question 2 (b), the best yield of syngas is attained if pressure is lowered
and temperature is increased.  Unfortunately, contradictory statements resulted to the loss of the second mark for the
explanation to justify why such conditions would increase the yield of syngas.

Some candidates gave multiple responses in questions that explicitly asked for one, such as Question 1.

This is problematic because there is no rationale for the long lists.  Candidates should think through their responses and
give the best possible answer rather than multiple answers.

In cases where the answer is not exact, candidates are required to round off their answers to match the accuracy in the
data provided.  However, as a rule of thumb, candidates may round off to 3 significant figures but only in the last stage
of the calculation i.e. for the value placed in the spaces provided for the answer.

Candidates should be reminded that whenever they are required to draw diagrams showing the shape of methane and
optical isomers, then three dimensional structures should be drawn. Non-superimposable mirror images should be
legibly drawn for optical isomers for question 5 (b).

The work this year was generally very neat and tidy.  However, some candidates did not completely erase their pencil
marks when they were altering their answers.  This was especially prevalent in chemical equations where Examiners
could make out the final number as well as in the organic structures.  Furthermore, candidates should be reminded that
any working out or attempts to answer a question that candidates do not wish the Examiner to read should be clearly
crossed out and re-written legibly.

Candidates are reminded of the need to read their questions carefully.  Underlining key words is generally helpful
for candidates to understand the demands of the question.  The importance of reading their answers cannot be
overemphasized to ensure they make the intended sense.

Answers should be written in the spaces provided.  The space provided is usually in excess to what the candidates
require.      Whenever   a   candidate   finds   that   the   space   provided   is   not   adequate,   it   usually   means   they   are   writing   too
much, unless they have an unusually big handwriting.  When boxes are provided for diagrams or structures, only the
final answer should be in the box. When more than one structure is provided it is difficult for Examiners to decide which
one if the final answer.

General comments

It is quite pleasing to report that there was a marked improvement in the quality of work in comparison to last year.  It
was also encouraging to note that candidates in some centres were very well prepared for the examinations and they
could give expected responses to most of the questions asked.  Teachers are encouraged to ensure that they prepare
their learners very well on all the specific objectives of the syllabus because it was quite clear that candidates from some
centres struggled to answer questions on certain topics of the syllabus such as Logic gates and circuits and algorithms.
This year, questions on algorithms proved to be the most difficult for most centres.  Teachers are therefore encouraged
to prepare their candidates very well on algorithms because, as it is stipulated in the syllabus, candidates should expect
questions on this topic every year.

General comments

Overall, there was an improvement in the quality of the candidates’ work compared to last year.

Questions that required an understanding of code were answered extremely well by some candidates. However,
candidates from some centres struggled to apply the knowledge and skills that Theme Three of the syllabus focuses on.

Candidates found questions beginning with “explain” more challenging as a more detailed response was expected for
full credit.

Precision and accuracy are expected in answers. Candidates should be prepared or assisted to achieve this.

The level of tidiness met the acceptable standard for all the candidates.

Most candidates made attempts to all questions.

It is highly recommended that teachers continue their excellent work and efforts.

GENERAL COMMENTS
Teachers are familiar with the content of the syllabus now guided and taught the candidates well to ensure that they
knew what to expect in the exam. Teachers should be applauded for the effort done to prepare the learners for the
examination.  According to the responses of the candidates, it is clear that the whole syllabus was covered by most
centres.

Thanks, should also go to other role players like the entire Ministry of Education, Regional Offices, Schools, Communities
and of course the Candidates who wrote this examination.

Very good responses were received from the centres regarding the quality and standard of the question paper. It could
be well interpreted regarding the style, language and graphics.

From the responses of the candidates on the questions, there were no problems answering the questions in general,
although in some cases candidates did not give the correct responses. However, for most questions and candidates
could score good marks.

Evidence also shows that quite a few candidates did not have the knowledge to answer certain questions successfully
and some did not attempt certain questions. By the spread of marks for this question paper, it appears that candidates
were generally well prepared.

Section A consisted of compulsory short questions across the syllabus. In most cases candidates scored good marks,
but in some cases candidates were not well prepared.

This year we had 55 candidates of which only a few candidates answered the Technology Part, only two candidates
answered  the  Communication  Part  and  the  rest  answered  the  Resistant  Part  in  Section  B  in  the  question  paper.  This
section was answered fairly well by most candidates.

In 2022, 60 candidates entered to write the exam, but in 2023 there are 56 candidates, of which one candidate was
absent. It is our expectation that in 2024 the number of candidates will be in line with the previous years.

                4.    Wear short sleeves, no ties or jewellery or loose fitting clothing while operating a
                      table saw.
                5.    Stand    comfortably,    with    your    feet    far    enough    apart    for    good    balance    and    wear
                      footwear with non-slip soles.
                6.    Use a push stick to cut stock that is 100 mm or less in width.

                      fence--this   can   be   as   simple   as   a   clamped   on   board   that   stops   just   before   the
                      saw blade, so that cut-off pieces cannot bind between blade and fence.
                8.    Position your body so that it is NOT in line with the blade, it keeps you out of the
                      line of most kick-backs.
                9.    Never reach behind or over the blade unless it has stopped turning.
                10.   Always disconnect the power before changing the blade or performing any other
                      maintenance operation.
                11.   Make sure that the blade has stopped turning before you adjust the table saw.
                12.   Always make sure that the blade is turning free before you turn on the power.
                13.   Keep the table top smooth and polished. A dirty or rough table requires you to use
                      more force to push the stock.
                14.   Never operate a table saw with the table insert removed.
                15.   Do  not  make  free-hand  cuts  on  a  table  saw.  Guide  the  stock  through  the  blade
                      using the rip fence or the mitre gauge.
                16.   Keep the blade guards, splitters and anti-kickback fingers in place and operating
                      freely. Check the action of these items before starting work.

                17.   The fence and the mitre gauge are not meant to be used together. Under some
                      circumstances, you can use both (see above on stop blocks), but the fence then
                      needs an auxiliary fence added. That fence or stop must end just before the saw
                      blade. Don’t mess with the fence adjustment when the saw is running.

   information, like: tools, construction, materials.

 (b) Specifications
   Candidates may not copy the specifications given in the paper.
   Generic responses must be avoided.  These specifications must be relatively specific. Some candidates
   stated generic specifications like “it must be safe, must look nice, etc.” Specifications must also be justified
   with reasoning.
   A specification could look as follows: E.g. “The product must be made out of aluminium, because it is light
   weight and does not corrode.”
   The following points should be covered in the specification:
   Functionality, ergonomics, aesthetics, materials and construction.

 (c) Design solutions
   Many ideas were not in line with the criteria given. Candidates should draw the ideas according to the
   specifications given.
   Ideas should also be drawn three dimensionally.
   Detail should be shown in the sketches, many notes should be written.
   Measurements should be added. More than three ideas should be drawn.
   Ideas should be adequately rendered / coloured and enhanced.
   The ideas should also be evaluated.

(d)    Development of proposed solution
              This is the part where candidates of some centres lost valuable marks. In this section of the question paper
              the candidates should take the chosen idea and make further detailed decisions on form, materials and
              construction methods to be used in the final product. In some cases, candidates did not do a sufficient
              development of the final idea.
              This is not simply a repetition of one of the ideas recorded in the previous section.
              The candidates should show processes that are to be followed in the manufacturing and also                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          show details
              of construction.
              Rendering / colouring should be done and measurements should be added.
              The development should also be evaluated.

       (e) Presentation
              Candidates of some centres just gave a single view with little or no detail or notes.
              The following is expected in this question.  An Isometric sketch or drawing with notes, and an
              Orthographic drawing including dimensions.
              Additional sketches can also be added to show construction detail.
              The isometric drawing or sketches should be rendered showing what the final product should look like.

Teachers      are      to      read      and      implement      these      comments      and      pointers      given.            This      will      ensure      a      better      mark      for      the
candidates in future.

GENERAL COMMENTS

Regions must be commended for efforts deployed to ensure the completion and submission of coursework samples
from all centres.

The quality of coursework for NSSCAS 2023 was generally good.  There were some centres that produced coursework
that is below average. This indicates that the candidates were not correctly guided by the teacher.  Regional Offices should
make sure that Examiner ’s Reports and Centre Reports are studied and recommendations drafted for implementation
purposes are forwarded from the regions to the schools.

Regional Office should visit schools that did not perform well and investigate what the reasons are for the submission of
substandard samples. In the cases where teachers are not sure what is expected in the folders, they should be trained
to ensure that the candidates can be taught how to compile a folder correctly.  On the other hand, if the teacher is not
performing, the principal and head of department at the school should be informed to continuously monitor the work
done by the teacher and the progress of the candidates on the project and folders.  If possible networking with DNEA,
NIED    and    other    regions    with    Senior    Education    Officers    as    well    as    relevant    stakeholders    should    be    initiated    to    have
teachers capacitated and assisted on a regular basis.  It appears that the common mistakes centres made, during 2022
were repeated in the 2023 design folder, because the learners were not taught correctly by the teacher.  This makes one
realise how many candidates are penalised for poor quality of work submitted, as some centres have not been putting in
the much needed efforts from the beginning of the Senior Secondary phase.  A conclusion could be drawn that Centre
Reports   are   not   studied   and   recommendations   not   implemented   by   many   centres.      Due   to   the   defiant   negligence   by
some centres, the assistance of the Senior Education Officers and Circuit Inspectors is needed to make sure that these
reports are studied, analysed and the recommendations are implemented.

Once again, the HOD’s are pleaded to take the responsibility of ensuring that folders and projects are monitored
throughout the year in future. Towards the end of the second term the folders should be internally moderated before the
marks  are  dispatched  to  DNEA  for  external  moderation.    Regional  Offices  must  make  sure  that  NSSCAS  schools  are
provided with the necessary materials and tools for candidates to build quality models.
DNEA observed that some centres’ projects were compromised by the lack of adequate resources.

Candidates        who        are        not        submitting        sufficient        photographic        evidence        is        a        problem        when        the        projects        have        to        be
moderated.  There were a few cases where candidates made poor problem selections and outcomes and showed little
evidence of imaginative interpretation and creativity.  The sample of work presented for moderation was suitable in most
cases and centres generally applied the assessment criteria appropriately, although, in some cases, this was not at the
correct level.

All folders must include clear photographic evidence of the artefacts, in addition to an overall view of the final
product, showing detail to support the awarding of marks.

COMMENTS ON SPECIFIC ASSESSMENT HEADINGS

Defining

Some of the candidates clearly stated the problem to be addressed but not all gave a concise Design Brief.  Candidates
should be encouraged to complete adequate and relevant research in order to form a suitable knowledge base after
formulating the Brief.  Only then can the specifications be listed.  These specifications must be relatively specific.  Many
candidates stated generic specifications like “it must be safe” or “must not be big or too small”, etc.  This research does
not only refer to materials and its properties.  Some candidates included points of specification but of a generic nature
which could be applied to any product.

Research

Some centres research consisted of irrelevant information that was simply written in a paragraph form.  This did not lead
the candidate to an idea of what the outcome of the product should be.

Candidates should do research into similar existing products as mentioned in the Design Brief and evaluate these
products regarding cost, material, etc.  This section should give clear and specific requirements for the design outcome

and   for   the   awarding   of   maximum   marks.      Then   additional   information   regarding   the   processes,   material   and   fittings
should be researched to see what is available locally.

Conceptualising

This is where candidates can show evidence of genuine design creativity.  Imaginative and innovative handling of good
range of concepts and ideas is of essence. Some candidates included a wide range of different ideas enhanced by clearly
annotated sketches.  Often candidates presented a few drawings that showed too little design capabilities and tended
to follow a single concept.  These ideas can be presented most successfully through sketches and candidates should
be encouraged to include everything that comes to mind. Annotations should include comments on the construction,
joining methods and materials.  Then it is important that the each idea is evaluated as to how an idea might link to the
specification.

Development

In this section of the folder the candidates should take only the chosen idea and make further detailed decisions on
form,   materials   and   construction   methods   to   be   used   in   the   final   product.   Ideas   should   be   fully   developed   with   good
attention to detail.  Candidates are expected to show deep insight and good command of related knowledge. In some
cases    candidates    found    it    difficult    to    apply,    and    in    these    cases    the    final    ideas    were    simply    a    repetition    of    one    of    the
ideas recorded in the previous section.  Candidates are expected to also illustrate every step of production with notes
describing the action.

In  most  cases  the  final  drawings  of  the  Design  Solution  were  generally  well-presented  and  gave  sufficient  information
with regards to the manufacturing of the product.

Presentation

Candidates  were  expected  to  show  refined  graphical  skills  including  fluent  freehand  and  precise  measured  drawings.
Most centres could produce drawings with good command of rendering and other enhancement which is commendable.
Centres in the top band produced excellent communication skills and had their work well managed and attractively laid
out.  Some centres did not give the correct drawings.

The following is expected:  An isometric drawing / sketch with dimensions and notes.  (Rendered), an exploded view
(rendered) an orthographic drawing showing detailed dimensions.  Then also a cutting list, other material list, a table
showing time planning and a flowchart showing the sequential steps of production.

Product realization (Control; Technical; Product)

Photographic evidence (photographic gallery) showed that some candidates were able to work on their own and able
to  work  at  an  acceptable  standard  of  construction  and  finish  to  the  extent  that  the  end  product  could  be  used.    Sadly,
some   centres   could   not   provide   sufficient   photographic   evidence   to   substantiate   the   credibility   of   the   folders.      Some
photographic evidence is just a mere posing activity and no real action is seen which made it difficult for the moderator
to clearly distinguish various safe approaches and processes from the photos.

Notably, photographic evidence showed some candidates operating power tools (such as angle grinders) without the
required protective clothing (leather gloves, eye protection), an unsafe practise that should be discouraged.

Clear photos of the candidate doing all the processes, as well as clear photos showing the final product.  The candidate
must be seen working in the pictures.

Testing and Evaluation

Some candidates included photographic evidence to show the testing of the product, which is commendable.  They are,
however, encouraged to link the outcome of the original specifications and make objective judgements on the success
of their products.  The section should also include suggestions for further modifications or possible future improvements.
Therefore   centres   are   implored   to   ensure   that   specifications   are   fully   evaluated   and   tested   in   this   section,   which   will
guarantee maximum marks for the candidates.

Conclusion

Even though the coursework received from the centres for NSSCAS was at a high standard in most cases, it is clear
that centres offering NSSCAS Design and Technology for 2024 as a subject need to get a unified training to standardize
the general understanding on the different sub-topics for the design folders.

          Analyse how the depreciation of a country’s                                   8
          currency is likely to influence the balance of trade of

          Kn (Up to 3 marks)
          •    A balance of trade is the record of receipts for
               visible exports and payments for visible imports
               between the residents of a country and the rest of
               the world in a specific period of time.
          •    Balance of trade is part of the current account of
               the balance of payments of a country.
          •    Depreciation is a decrease in:  the price of
               one currency in terms of another currency or its
               international price caused by market forces.
          Ap (Up to 2 marks)
          •    Depreciation of currency will make exports
               cheaper
          •    and imports more expensive in terms of foreign
               currencies.
          An (Up to 3 marks)                                                                    No marks awarded for surplus of
          •    Domestic firms will be able to sell more visible                                 balance of trade.

          •    Import countries by pay less of their currency for the

          •    Improve credit side of trade balance.
          •    Imported visible products might become too
               expensive.
          •    Imports are likely to decrease. (Pay more domestic
               currency to get the same number/fewer products.)
          •    Reduce deficit on trade balance.
          •    Imported visible goods that cannot be produced in

          •    Depreciation improves balance of trade on condition

3    POSITIVE SUGGESTIONS TO TEACHERS
     Learners should:
     •     Know and understand economic terminology and theories.
     •     Be able to interpret economic data.
     •     Use the tools of economic analysis and evaluation.
     •     Express economic ideas logically and clearly.
     •     Apply economic understanding to current economic issues from a variety of economies.

POSITIVE SUGGESTIONS TO TEACHERS
Teachers	should	warn	learners	that	there	is	only	one	statement	which	is	the	correct	answer	in	Section	A:	Part	1	(Multiple
Choice).	There	are	always	distractors	which	might	make	them	think	twice	about	their	choice,	and	then	they	need	to
spend	more	time	on	thinking	the	options	through.
Learners	should	be	taught/guided	to	write	in	their	own	words	as	far	as	possible.	Teachers	should	expose	learners	to	as
many	reading	comprehension	passages	and	questions	as	possible.	They	should	as	well	expose	learners	to	directed
writing	activities	and	help	the	learners	to	identify	relevant	content	ideas.	Candidates	must	be	reminded	that	their	scripts
speak	for	themselves	and	must	ensure	that	their	responses	are	clear.
Learners	should	be	guided	on	how	to	respond	to	SECTION	B	and	empowered	with	the	correct	techniques	of	answering
the	question.	Teachers	could	also	spend	more	time	on	practising	sentence	structure	with	their	learners.	Candidates
struggle	to	express	their	ideas	clearly	in	meaningful	sentences.		Learners	should	be	encouraged	to	write	in	full	sentences

and	grammatically	correct	ones.	Some	candidates	wrote	(used)	capital	letters	in	the	middle	of	the	sentence.	Punctuation
is	an	essential	part	of	writing.	Therefore,	it	should	not	be	neglected	at	this	level.	Teachers	should	consider	teaching
spelling	and	grammar	in	general.
There	should	be	a	deliberate	focus	on	teaching	learners	about	sense	of	voice.	They	must	know	who	they	are	writing

General comments

Candidates’ essays were not of a good standard as expected for AS level. Many candidates should not have taken
English as a Second Language on AS level.  The questions were clear and could be easily interpreted.  The candidates
who should have been on this level understood the questions and managed to provide substantial and relevant content.
It   was   evident   that   some   candidates   worked   out   an   essay   on   a   specific   theme   beforehand.     They   tried   to   fit   it   in   with
the  theme  and  totally  ignored  the  instructions  under  the  specific  theme  i.  e.  Conservation  as  theme.  Some  discussed
conservation in general instead of answering the question which clearly required a narrative about a visit to see how
their families conserve and protect.  Thus, many candidates misinterpreted the topics albeit intentionally or not.  They
should be taught to read the instructions carefully and make sure they stay on the topic while developing their plots.

A few candidates ignored the clear instructions that Part 1 is always compulsory and instead opted to write two pieces
both taken from Part 2.  This resulted in no marks for the first essay and only the second piece marked.

The biggest concern in 2023 (this year) was the language usage.  Many candidates struggled with sentence structure
and appropriate vocabulary.

There    was    a    significant     improvement    in    candidates    adhering    to    word    count.    Thank    you    for    that.    It    is    still    a    concern
though that many centres blatantly ignore the clear instruction that the length of a piece had to be between 220 and
260 words.  That resulted in excessively long pieces where candidates actually penalised themselves since ideas were
repeated and structures started to fall apart. Candidates must adhere to the prescribed word count.

Part 1 of this paper is compulsory and the majority of candidates understood and adhered to the requirements of
the  topic.    Candidates  need  thorough  training  on  how  to  adhere  to  specific  instructions  and  answer  all  aspects  of  the
question.  Candidates have to be encouraged to gather as much information as possible regarding the specific fields for
that specific year which will enable them to write mature and convincing plots.

The majority of centres realised that “idiom” refers to aspects such as style, tone, language in general and the excessive
use of idioms was avoided this year.

The use of contractions is still a concern.  Candidates still experienced problems with word formation, inappropriate use
of participles, incorrect spelling, punctuation and sentence structure. Those mistakes had tremendously affected the
overall quality of candidates’ essays.

Candidates have to be encouraged to read in order to gain general knowledge, specifically with regards to the themes
for 2024.  A lack of general knowledge resulted in mundane and unconvincing plots, lacking good arguments and
extensive examples.

Many essays were presented very slovenly.  This impeded easy reading and understanding of candidates’ plots which
might have resulted in an avoidable poor mark.

Some candidates could write convincing plots presented in a neat manner.

Comments on individual questions
Part 1
Topic 1   Culture

Young people in Namibia no longer honour their cultural heritage, but instead follow global trends and traditions.

To what extent do you agree with this statement?

This topic was compulsory.  Most candidates could answer this topic, with varied success.  It was expected of
candidates to discuss this in general or provide examples proving that young people do/do not follow their cultural
norms    anymore.        Most    candidates    referred    to    the    influence    of    social    media    and    peers    and    were    able    to    provide    an
example of two.  Very few candidates could write convincing and substantiated arguments on this topic. Most plots

lacked  mature  thinking.    Weaker  candidates  wrote  essays  on  technology  and  how  it  influences  the  youth.    Some  also
listed examples of cultural activities without elaborating on or indicating how the youth still embrace or disregard them.
Stronger candidates were able to create a link between the contemporary times and the past to show how the youth no
longer honour their cultural heritage.  Some candidates only defined what culture is throughout the essay, which resulted
in poor marks.  A few mature and convincing essays were presented containing relevant examples and arguments.

Part 2
Topic 2   Conservation

You visited your family who live in a large village.  They are actively involved in community conservation that grew out of
their recognition that wildlife and other natural resources are essential in improving their living standards.

Relate your experiences during that visit and the lessons you learned regarding the importance of conservation.

This was not a popular choice. For this question candidates had to elaborate on a visit to their family and what they
learned regarding conservation during that visit.  Many candidates misinterpreted the topic and elaborated either on
conservation in general or their visit. Others struggled to come up with tangible examples of conservational activities,
because they are perhaps not even aware of any.  Many referred to conservancies and families who worked for Nature
Conservation.  Stronger candidates wrote well sustained plots with convincing and relevant examples.

Topic 3   Advertising and marketing

After saving for a while, you ordered a much desired item online.  However, when it arrived you were very disappointed
and had been clearly misled by the advertisement.

Tell your story.

This was a popular choice.  Candidates had to write a story on how they had ordered an item online with money saved
and once received the item was different from the one advertised.  Most candidates answered this successfully as they
exhibited sound knowledge and understanding of the requirements.  Some stories contained lovely and unexpected
twists which resulted in high marks. Some plots involved complex ideas.  Weaker candidates wrote insubstantial plots
containing mundane ideas and uninteresting references.  Some candidates ended up discussing the advantages of
advertising and marketing for a business while some weaker candidates elaborated so extensively on saving for the
article that they ran out of words when the actual item arrived.  That resulted in lame development and poor marks.

Topic   4   Food and drink

Mankind needs food to survive.  It should, therefore, not be a concern where it comes from or how it is produced.  Do
you agree or disagree?

This topic was rather a challenge to the few candidates who opted for it.  For many, instead of presenting an argument
on whether people should be concerned where their food or drink comes from or how it is produced or not, they offered
superfluous   accounts   about   why   food   is   essential   for   survival.      Some   only   referred   to   genetic   modification   processes
without linking them to why they are harmful or not to mankind and the environment.  Stronger candidates presented
complex ideas, showing concern when it came to GM, preservatives and hygiene.  Some candidates concentrated on
only the first part of the question, missing the second part completely.  Some referred to theft as a method of survival.
All in all, only a few candidates were able to produce mature, substantial and convincing plots.

Topic 5   Free time activities

Modern life is about work and no play, resulting in unhappy people with unhealthy lifestyles.  What are your views?

Many candidates opted for this topic with varied success.  Candidates should have discussed whether people today do
not  maintain  a  balance  between  work  and  leisure  so  eventually  are  unhappy  or  unhealthy.    Many  candidates  defined
leisure time and wrote extensive plots on the importance of leisure and provided many examples of leisure time activi-
ties.  The topic was not about leisure time.  Some candidates discussed why it is important to work without considering
the fact that they were supposed to discuss the need for a balance between work and play.  This resulted in them
scoring marks in the lower bands.  Stronger candidates executed this topic well.  They were able to link ideas and argu-
ments in a convincing way.

Positive suggestions to teachers
•    More time should be spent on the construction of sentences and the different types of sentences i. e simple,
     complex and compound.  Teachers should teach grammar and language usage as a crucial component of English,
     concentrating on specific problematic areas such as concord, punctuation and effective vocabulary.  Spelling tests
     should be written on a regular basis.  Vocabulary quizzes should be part of weekly exercises.  Learners may mark
     each other ’s essays, awarding marks according to the mark scheme and discuss the outcome with each other.  In
     this way they also familiarise themselves with the requirements of the mark scheme.  Good essays should also be
     shared with others.
•    Encourage learners to read in order for them to gain general knowledge, which will enable them to write convincing
     and sustained plots. Through reading they build up a wide range of sophisticated vocabulary. However, they
     should not use it randomly and excessively. Argumentative essays require convincing and sustained facts. It is,
     therefore, essential for learners to expand their general knowledge.  Teachers should cover all the fields thoroughly.
     Candidates    should   be   encouraged   to   do   research    on   the   various    fields.      If   they   have   sufficient   knowledge    of   all
     fields, they will be able to write both narrative and argumentative essays.
•    Numbers up to twenty should be written out in words, whereas numbers above twenty and dates should be written
     in numerals.
•    Emphasis must be put on word count.  When word count is exceeded, most candidates lose focus, structure and
     relevance.
•    Candidates must not create their own topics.  They should just indicate their choice, i.e. 2. Conservation.

     Vir die digterlike proses is slypwerk nodig.  Die digterlike proses het die vermoë om die ganse werklikheid oop te
     breek, “aan twee”, en die ganse werklikheid van die aarde en alles wat daarop is te verken; selfs die buiteruimtes
     en die goddelike.  Die aardse en die boweaardse.
     BEELDE:
     Die beiteltjie word die simbool van die taal waardeur die digterskap tot stand kom.  Die digter het die
     verantwoordelikheid om sy taalvermoë te ontwikkel.
     In die poësie word ganse werklikheid verken. –          “val die planeet aan twee”; “bars van my beitel af dwarsdeur
     die sterre loop”

2 “Woorde”         deur Vincent Oliphant [1998]
     Die digter besin ook oor die mag van woorde.  Die mag is volgens hom beperk.  Sy woorde in sy verse werk ook nie
     gewelddadig nie: “nie die byt van koeëls en grofgeskut nie” Baie betrokke poësie is dikwels fel krities.  Hierdie
     digter volg die weg van biddende, pleitende woorde eerder as geweld om verandering te bewerkstellig.  Hy pleit
     dat mens mekaar sal aanvaar as medemense in liefde: “woorde kan bloot bid en pleit en wens” Hy pleit dit vir
     SA, maar ook universeel vir ander mense.
     Die digter se taak is dus om mense op te roep om te verander en lief te hê, eerder as om te kritiseer en
     onvergenoegdheid te verwoord.

3    “by toccata en fuga in d mineur”            Marlene van Niekerk
     Die titel van die gedig verwys na ’n grootse Bachkomposisie vir die orrel.  Dis ’n majestueuse kunswerk.  Die
     titel verwys dus reeds na die kreatiewe of skeppende proses by wyse van die orrelwerk en musiekstuk.  In die
     gedig word besin watter groteske gebeure nodig was vir die totstandkoming van die orrelskepping.  Volgens die
     spreker moes die komponis teenwoordig gewees het by God se eie skeppingsproses van die aarde.  God se
     skeppingsproses moes die komponis aangeraak het om sy bladmusiek/orrelstuk te skep.  Die skeppingsproses is
     ’n grootse fratsgebeure waarby die goddellike kreatiwiteit en skeppingsgebeure ingesluit is.  Die kreatiewe proses
     word dus verbind aan die goddelike skeppingsproses self.

4    “Digter wordende”         Antjie   Krog
     Die ganse talende en verwoordende skeppingsproses het met klank, die sintuie en die ervaring van die digter te
     make.  Die digter verwoord sy/haar ervaring deur die lyf en sintuie in klank, woorde en taal.  Die vers kom uit haar
     wese en menswees – die digter dig met haar tong sy haal asem  - ja, diep uit haar oor.  Die totstandkoming kom
     uit die digter se asemhaling en gehoor tot stand; alle sintuie.

Eerste liefde Elisabeth Eybers
Beeldspraak speel die deurslaggewende rol in die vers.  Die ganse gedig berus op die vergelyking tussen die eerste
liefde en ’n jong onskuldige meisie wat sterf.  Die liefde het dus voor volwassewording en ryping tot niet gegaan.  Ander
beelde wat by die jeugdigheid van die meisie aansluit, is die verwysing na die “oggendstond”             die oggenduur of die
begin van die dag.  Dieselfde kan gesê word van die “lentegras” en die “voorjaarsgrond”

Dis alles natuurbeelde van die begin van die seisoen; die eerste gebeure van die seisoen soos hierdie dan ook die
eerste liefde is.
Die spreker en die geliefde begrawe die gestorwe meisie of liefde.  Hierdie meisie en liefde was “tingerig-fyn”; met
“slank en ligte vingers”,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 “’n sagte stem en blou wonder-oë”              Die oë verwys na die verwondering wat dikwels met
die eerste liefde gepaard gaan – ook die onopgesmuktheid.

Die spreker wonder of die eertydse geliefde ook soms aan die liefde dink.  Sy weet sy mag nie ween nie, maar staan

eerste liefde.  Die beelde waarmee die meisie/liefde beskryf word, gee erkenning aan die spesiale jeugdige skoonheid
van die eerste liefdeservaring.

        Paper 1



As mentioned in the 2021 report, there were still a number of candidates who struggled with the time constraints of
the paper.  This led to incomplete responses which had a detrimental effect on their marks.  It might be a good idea to
practise time management in class.

Generally, the SPAG (spelling and grammar) errors were fewer this year.   However, a good number of candidates will
still benefit by paying more attention to this and perhaps being motivated to edit their work.

Continuous awareness of audience and purpose needs some work.

Paper 1 (Writing paper)

Question 1 (a)   Blog
The candidates were requested to write an advisory blog for the Grade 8s who are soon to be their juniors in high school.

Even though the majority were able to write a decent response to this question, a number of candidates still struggled
with the advisory style.  Furthermore, most of the candidates did not adhere to any of the conventions of a blog save
the conversational style.

Except for some (the minority) whose style was too formal for this blog, most adapted an informal style.  Nonetheless,
candidates should still be made aware of the difference between informal and conversational style.

Not only will candidates benefit from alternating their sentence structures (minor sentence, simple, complex, complex-
compound and compound sentences) and sentence types (declaratives, interrogatives, exclamations and imperatives)
for effect  to score higher marks, but they will also be better prepared to write their reflective commentaries.

In addition, using punctuation for effect will help the candidates to improve their marks. Some candidates in the lower
bands relied heavily on run-on sentences in a bid to bring out sophisticated ideas.

The above will already assist the candidates to adopt a more conversational style and provide a more nuanced piece of
writing which will reflect a stronger sense of voice.

Even though, there was a clear improvement in establishing a clear audience, it was still a problem in certain centres.
It could already be established in the introduction that the audience is young teenagers.  It might be beneficial to teach
the candidates how to maintain the expected style.

Overall, there was a definite improvement in the approach to question 1 (a).  Continue to teach them how to analyse the
questions properly, constantly keeping the audience and purpose in mind. When candidates understand how to bring
about the effect, it will be easy to comment on Question 1 (b).

Question 1 (b)
There was also a clear improvement in the approach to this question.  It is clear that the teachers felt more comfortable
teaching the reflective commentary to their candidates.  However, form is still somewhat neglected in their writing.  This
might be due to the fact that candidates did not really apply many or any form aspects when writing their blogs.

Perhaps, it might help to think about form as ‘what stands out’ when you look at the text:

•     punctuation marks (exclamations, question marks etc.),
•     headings and subheadings,
•     repetition,
•     sentence structure (minor sentences, one-word sentences etc.) and
•     paragraph structures (very short paragraphs, longer paragraphs) etc.
On AS level, candidates are expected to use all their form aspects for effect.  If they plan this when responding to
Question     1     (a),     they     will     definitely     be     able     to     reflect     on     their     use     in     the     reflective     commentary     and     their     marks     will
increase accordingly.

Structure (development within the essay) can be viewed as the building blocks of the responses. Without it no essay can
stand. It is imperative to zoom into it deeply then build form and language therein. More needs to be done in practice so
that it is embedded in candidates before they sit for the final paper.

One      of      the      biggest      pet      peeves      was      the      incorrect      identification       of      devices      and      their      effects.            It      seemed      like      some
candidates just provided generic effects which did not match their text at all.  Thus, they could seldomly be credited
for these responses. Precision needs to be of high regard so as to  be exhaustive in articulation ultimately creating a
sophisticated response.

SECTION B
It is such a pity that there are still candidates who did not complete these responses or did not meet the length
requirements of the question, with some learners writing even fewer than 250 words.  As a result, they had to be marked
down due to a rubric infringement which cost them an entire band in their writing.

Question 2
More than 75% of the candidates responded to this question.  Unfortunately, the ending of the narrative was generally
poorly answered.  The narrative definitely needs more attention in class.    The lack of question analysis (probably due to
the lack of time management) was very clear as only about 10% of the responses focused on the ending of a narrative.

On top of this, most candidates who wrote complete narratives did not even incorporate any falling action.  Even though
the majority of narratives ended with a climax and a conclusion, they omitted the falling action entirely.

The narrative on AS level requires a more nuanced response than most candidates were able to produce.  In fact, the
narrative might be more challenging than the other questions since many a candidate lacked the narrating style as they
opted to write  an entire report on what happened instead.  These candidates lacked sophisticated lexis, punctuation,
sentence structures and types as well as paragraph variety for effect.

EXPRESSIONS:

Lexis
Even though the expressions were mostly clear, they were not always relevant.  Common lexis frequented the responses
and could not be considered sophisticated.  Candidates should use more descriptive lexis, like verbs, adjectives,
adverbs etc.

Sentences structures
A great number of responses mostly repeated their sentence structures throughout their responses.  This led to
monotonous reading which lacked the impact of a proper narrative.  Variation of sentence structures and types (see
above) for effect should receive more attention.

Accuracy
Generally, the errors did not impede communication.  Editing should help eradicate this problem. Most candidates who
are still struggling with this aspect should be advised to rather write the second language examination.

TEXT ORGANISATION AND DEVELOPMENT
Marks were affected by the incorrect approach as most candidates did not develop the falling action but the entire essay.

It was expected that candidates start their responses no earlier than with the climax.  They could also have started their
response with the paragraph directly after the climax.  From there the falling action should have been developed clearly.
The conclusion is also important.

Candidates should also practise to balance show and tell better in their narratives.

PURPOSE AND AUDIENCE
Since it is a narrative, the audience requires an informal style with sophisticated expressions. The informal style was
mostly clear.  However, the sophisticated expressions need attention.

The purpose was generally not met as the candidates did not only focus on the ending of the narrative.  In fact, most
responses did not even reflect any falling action at all.

Question 3
Two contrasting letters to the press were requested.  This question was answered with more success than the narrative.
However, the responses mostly lacked specificity.

It is advised that learners are taught to focus more on their persuasive tone and the audience of the piece.

The format of the letter to the press was often omitted.

EXPRESSION:
Unfortunately, many of these letters were merely informative and lacked the persuasive approach that was requested.
The learners also struggled with the more formal register of the letters.  Two clear voices had to be established.  Being
exposed to the difference between formal and informal writing might be beneficial to the candidates.

Sophisticated lexis, the variation of complex sentence structures and types as well as rhetorical devices were expected
in these responses.

ORGANISATION AND  DEVELOPMENT
These responses require the candidates to focus on one argument per paragraph.  Each argument needs to be backed
up with evidence (examples, statistics, anecdotes etc.).  If a candidate doesn’t have ample knowledge of the topic, they
should be dissuaded from responding to this question.  Specificity will definitely generate a more effective response.

PURPOSE AND AUDIENCE
The audience requires sophisticated lexis, a more formal register and a strong voice.

Purpose was not always met as some of the letters struggled to create a strong voice and merely wrote informative
responses.

Question 4
The evaluative report seemed to have been the most approachable question.  It was also the second most popular
question of this section.

EXPRESSION
Candidates had to use informal register as the audience is the school community.  This was easily attainable.
Unfortunately, the evaluative style fell by the wayside, and informative responses were more frequent.  Thus, the
purpose was often not met.  Practising an evaluative style will be beneficial to the candidates.

ORGANISATION AND  DEVELOPMENT
If they refer to the crowning of Mr and Ms Valentine, they were expected to mention who was crowned.  Many a times,
these essays were very general in their responses.  Once again, the development lacked specificity which deemed them
less effective.

LANGUAGE
Only a limited number of candidates used sophisticated expressions and were able to write aesthetically appealing
essays.  In fact, grammar deserves more attention in the class room.

The following common errors should be avoided in future:

Malapropisms, punctuation errors, sentence constructions, commonly confused words.

Tautology was all too common:   more easier and utmost best were still common problems.

GENERAL
It might be a good idea to have the learners practise time management more to establish their speed of analysing and
responding to this paper.  Where some candidates wrote insightful and complete responses, the majority struggled to
reach the word limits.

It seems like there are still too many candidates in the First Language class that do not belong there.

Candidates can benefit from practising, teaching and exposing them

•    to the use of discourse markers for improved cohesion;
•    to the different levels of formality in writing;
•    to the different conventions (esp. form conventions) of the pieces;
•    to rules of language;
•    to question analysis;
•    to variation of punctuation, sentence structures and types as well as paragraphs.
We commend all the AS level teachers on a job well done!  A huge improvement was seen across the country.  We
sincerely wish that this advice assists all teachers in doing an even better job in 2024.

Key messages
•	                       Option	(A)	discursive	essays	should	analyse	specific	details	of	the	text	within	the	argument	presented.
•	                       Option	(B)	passage	questions	may	usefully	place	the	passage	in	the	wider	text	as	a	relevant	context.

General comments
The	general	standard	was	pleasing	with	the	large	majority	of	candidates	showing	a	sound	knowledge	and	understanding
of	the	set	texts.	Most	responses	reflected	an	improvement	in	time	management.	Only	a	few	candidates	did	not	complete
the	paper.	There	were	also	a	few	candidates	who	attempted	three	questions.	Please	note	that	candidates	are	expected
to	answer	two	questions	from	two	different	genres	only.	Centres	should	expose	their	candidates	to	old	papers	so	that
they	do	not	get	confused	during	the	exam	session.

In	addition,	most	students	wrote	lengthy	answers.	A	huge	improvement	from	last	year.	The	quality	of	expression	was
sound	in	most	cases,	but	there	are	still	too	many	candidates	that	displayed	expressive	weaknesses	which	can	impede
communication	at	this	level.

There	were	only	a	few	responses	on	the	dramas	As you like it, and Woza Albert! while	short	stories	were	less	popular
this	year.	 	The	novels,	All The Bright Places and Life & Times of Michael K	were	favoured	with	poetry	remaining	the
most	popular	genre.	Answers	reflecting	a	wide	range	of	performance	were	seen	on	each	of	the	texts	attempted	by	the
candidates.

Furthermore,	there	were	a	number	of	answers	based	on	the	passage	questions	where	the	candidates	seemed	to	have
little	knowledge	of	the	textual	context	or	understanding	of	its	significance	to	the	wider	text.	At	this	level	of	assessment,
it	is	fundamental	to	a	successful	answer	that	candidates	will	know	their	texts	well	and	have	some	understanding	of
the	 basic	elements	     of	 the	 text	in	 its	genre.	For	instance,	       not	 one	  candidate	   could	  identify	 the	satire	in	   the	extract
from	the	short	story	The	Contest,	which	is	a	fundamental	element	in	the	story.	Most	candidates	who	attempted	this
question	could	not	write	a	solid	answer	on	the	significance	of	the	extract.	Therefore,	without	the	necessary	knowledge
and	understanding	as	basis	on	which	to	build	an	interpretation,	the	essays	were	often	generalised	and	restricted	and
severely	limited.

Moreover,	candidates	should	always	spend	some	time	in	planning	their	response	and	deciding	what	material	is	relevant
to	their	interpretation	before	beginning	to	write	their	essay.	The	lack	of	planning	might	lead	to	no	thesis	statement	or
introduction	at	the	opening	of	an	essay	which	limits	appropriate	focus	on	the	given	task.

Assessment	Objective	L2	from	the	Literature	in	English	syllabus	states	that	candidates	should	‘analyse	ways	in	which
writers’	choices	of	language,	form	and	structure	shape	meanings	and	effects’.	Candidates	attempting	option (B)	passage
questions	often	did	not	adhere	to	meeting	this	Assessment	Objective	in	their	responses	to	the	given	passage.	They
often	only	wrote	a	narrative	summary	or	paraphrased	the	extract,	instead	of	focusing	on	the	ways	in	which	writers	use
language,	form	and	structure	to	shape	meaning.	Moreover,	this	also	applied	for	those	candidates	attempting	option
(A)	questions,	the	discursive	essay,	since	they	seldom	provided	evidence	that	they	were	able	to	do	this,	by quoting
or referring closely to specific moments	in	the	text.	Therefore,	irrespective	of	choosing	option (A)	or	(B)	candidates
should	discuss	all	references	in	detail,	focusing	on	the	writer’s	choices	and	exploring	what	for	the	candidate	are	the
effects	of	those	choices.

Candidates	responding	to	option	(B)	passage	questions,	                   who	briefly	place	the	passage	           within	 the	 wider	work	it	is
selected	from,	often	write	more	focused	and	relevant	answers.	Some	candidates	could	benefit	from	considering	this
approach,	as	it	will	give	a	context	to	their	interpretation	of	the	passage	itself,	as	well	as	providing	evidence	of	knowledge
of	the	text.	This	equally	applies	to	passages	from	poetry	selections	as	well	as	the	drama	texts.

Furthermore, rhetorical questions should be limited                   	as	  a	literary	  essay	  focuses	on	     analyses	   of	 the	 given	  text.
Candidates	    should	   focus	  on	the	  ways	the	    writers	  use	language,	form	and	style	          to	 create	meaning.	      If	a	candidate
continuously	uses	“then”	it	reflects	a	narrative	summary	or	paraphrase	of	the	given	text.	Moreover,	the	focus	should
not	be	confused	with	writing	an	analytical	essay	based	on	style,	structure	and	language.	The	focus	in	a	literary	essay	is
always	on	the	way	writers	present	the	text,	not	on	who	the	target	audience	is	or	the	main	purpose	of	the	text.

up.	Few	candidates	acknowledged	the	shift	from	Robert’s	direct	words	to	K’s	thoughts,	neither	the
           symbolism	of	standing	against	           the	wire	looking	out	      over	the	veld	–	suggesting	K’s	longing	to	be
           free.	Weak	answers	lost	focus	of	the	question	and	made	no	reference	to	the	way	in	which	Coetzee
           presents	Michael	K’s	thoughts,	but	rather	paraphrased	the	passage.	Better	answers	at	this	level	did

           in	the	camp	digging	“a	great	hole”	whereas	only	a	few	candidates	recognised	the	link	to	the	important
           theme	of	farming.	The	idea	that	Michael	K’s	thoughts	are	metaphorically	a	seed,	growing	and	getting
           stronger,	creating	fear	and	tension	as	realisation	dawns	                 on	Michael	K.	More	        competent	answers
           looked	at	the	presentation	in	detail,	showing	understanding	of	Coetzee’s	use	of	imagery	and	sensory

           K	builds	with	nature	and	with	the	soil,	which	is	reflected	in	the	extract.’,	continuing	to	successfully

Positive suggestions to teachers
•	   Teachers	should	discourage	students	to	use	superfluous	expressions	such	as	“brilliant	author”,	“exceptional	use	of
     imagery”	or	“the	author’s	wonderful	use	of	lexis”	These	expressions	are	arbitrary	and	does	not	constitute	a	personal
     response.
•	   Whenever	a	reference	is	made	to	literary	techniques	such	as	the	structure	of	the	poem,	rhyme	and	rhythm,	imagery
     or	pathos	or	ethos,	it	is	imperative	that	the	student	gives	a	reason	why	it	is	important.	They	have	to	focus	on	very
     specific	effects	created.
•	                                               Teachers should instruct students not to start their answers with a quote. It	is	better	to	teach	students	to	start
     their	writing	with	a	solid thesis statement,	which	they	then	continue	to	prove	by	using	strong points,	evidence
     and analysis     .
•	   Also	note	that	when	analysing	an	extract	or	poem,	it	is	imperative	to	focus	on	the	entire	text.	If	a	poem	has	four
     stanzas,	the	importance	of	all	the	stanzas	in	relation	to	the	task	need	to	be	discussed.	Moreover,	when	answering
     the	(b)	part	of	the	question	paper,	candidates	should	not	rely	heavily	on	parts	outside	the	given	extract.
•	   It	is	not	necessary	at	this	level	to	explain	literary	devices.	Rather	discuss	the	effect	created	by	the	specific	image
     than	wasting	time	to	give	a	definition	of	it.
•	   Lastly,	teach	the	candidates	to	refrain	from	counting	words.	There	is	no	word	limit	and	it	wastes	valuable	time.

In this paper in Teil A, Aufgabe 1 is compulsory.  This question consists of two parts, (a) and (b).  Learners were
required  to  write  a  biography  about  a  living  or  an  imaginary  person,  focusing  also  on  the  strengths  and  weaknesses.
Three of the learners created a biography about one of their parents.  The format of a biography was well maintained.
The other two learners picked a well-known person or an imaginary one.  All five completed the task satisfactorily.  All
learners provided a good reflective commentary (b) on their own written work stemming from (a).  The trend of delivering
differential quality in (a) and (b) was observed this year again, as all learners achieved higher marks for the (b) part of
Aufgabe 1.  The language skills among the learners were of a similar standard.
Thereafter the candidates are offered three options in Teil B.  One topic has to be answered.  Three candidates chose
Aufgabe 2 and two Aufgabe 3.  Aufgabe 4 was not considered by any of the candidates, most probably because they
found the contents of Aufgabe 2 and 3 more appealing to them.

Aufgabe 2
Nach langer Zeit der Dürre wird Namibia endlich mit ausdauernden und reichlichen Regenfällen gesegnet. Versetzen Sie

Sie auch seine Gefühle, die von der Zeit der Dürre und von Zukunftserwartungen geprägt sind.

sollten anerkannt werden.

Aufgabe 2 was a diary entry by a farmer about the past drought and the new rainy season, what he / she had learned
from the past years and what he / she would do differently in the future.  The feelings about future prospects had to be
